question.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -5 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}-3\cdot (2{x}_{3})+{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=5{x}_{3}.
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}5{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-9)\cdot 5+(-5)\cdot 2+(-5)\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-60\,}{\,\,\,30\,}b \\  & =-2b \\  & =-2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
